prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Please help! Tokyo sun looks wilty… i gave it water once over almost a month. Maybe quarter cup of water and let it air dry. I do have limited sun exposure at home.

Fyi soil is a little dry but im afraid to over water it..

So should i just take it out and give it water only on the lower part? Or repot it?

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
Your plant looks **underwatered and short on light**. The soil is dry, it got very little water over a month, and the stems look stretched and pale, which is typical of a plant reaching for more light.

**Watering:** Don't be afraid to water it properly. Give it a thorough soak until water runs out the drainage holes, then let it drain fully. Don't leave it sitting in the decorative bowl, since standing water can cause root rot. If you prefer, you can bottom-water by setting the pot in a tray of water for 20 to 30 minutes, then letting it drain. Afterward, water again only when the top inch or so of soil is dry.

**Light:** This is probably the bigger issue. Move it to the brightest spot you have, ideally a south- or west-facing window. If that isn't possible, a basic LED grow light running 12 to 14 hours a day will help a lot. Plants usually recover from low light over a few weeks, so expect slow improvement rather than an immediate change.

**Repotting:** Don't repot it right now. Stressed plants do better when left alone. Wait until it's actively growing again and the roots are crowding the pot.

I can't confirm the exact species from this photo, and the label is hard to read. If you can share a clearer picture of the label or the plant's leaves, I can tell you more about its specific needs.
